components.text: Explain what supplies the objective standard and intrinsic worth behind categorical moral reasons.
Explain why human beings and their harms possess objective rather than merely contingent value.
Explain what makes purportedly objective moral reasons and human worth objectively valuable rather than merely asserted.
Explain why persons who can be harmed or helped possess objective moral worth under naturalism.
Show why ideal rational agreement produces genuine obligation rather than convention.
Determine whether objective moral requirements need a personal source of authoritative commands.
Show why rational social agreement yields genuine categorical obligations rather than revisable human conventions.
Show why genuine moral duties require authoritative personal commands rather than impersonal normative requirements.
Explain the morally relevant distinction between reflective persons and nonreflective animals under naturalism.
Explain what distinguishes morally responsible human agents from nonreflective animals on a naturalistic account.
Answer why naturalistic reflective capacities are insufficient without a supernatural ground.
Explain how reasons and standards can guide conduct without an additional divine command.
Explain whether naturalistic reflective capacities require an additional supernatural ingredient for moral wrongness.
Show that identifying reflective capacities explains why those capacities and persons are objectively valuable.
Distinguish an explanation of responsible agency from an explanation of objective worth.
Explain why reflective capacities and the persons possessing them have objective value rather than merely being identifiable natural features.
Distinguish explaining responsible capacities from explaining the objective authority and value attached to those capacities.
Show why categorical moral reasons cease to matter merely because all life eventually ends.
Explain why present harms and benefits lack significance unless they alter the universe's final state.
Explain why finite harms and benefits cease to matter objectively merely because the universe eventually reaches extinction.
Show why desire-independent moral reasons require enduring cosmic consequences or postmortem accountability.
Show why torture lacks significance unless it changes the universe's eternal endpoint.
Identify why identical eventual cosmic outcomes do not entail that present torture and its effects lack objective significance.
Explain why prudential self-interest defeats rather than merely conflicts with overriding categorical moral reasons.
Show why finite harms lose moral authority when wrongdoing can serve the agent's interests.
Show why moral reasons cannot rationally outweigh conflicting prudential self-interest on a secular account.
Explain why reflective agents cannot act rationally on moral reasons when doing so conflicts with self-interest.
Show that conflict between morality and self-interest entails that prudence rationally overrides morality.
Identify why conflict between morality and prudence does not establish that prudential self-interest rationally trumps morality.
Demonstrate that secular contractual rules can yield objective condemnation rather than mere social convention.
Show that rationally constrained agreement prohibits serious wrongdoing despite an offender's interests.
Show that ideal rational agreement can generate objective condemnation rather than merely report prevailing social convention.
Show why ideal rational condemnation of Nazi killing requires a transcendent divine standard.
Answer the claim that genuine objective requirements need no personal lawgiver.
Show why the secular contract criterion cannot objectively condemn atrocities without a transcendent divine standard.
Explain why categorical reasons cannot support transcultural criticism unless grounded in God.
Explain how ultimate accountability remains consistent when repentant evildoers may avoid personally bearing punishment.
Clarify whether the proposed theistic system consistently holds serious wrongdoers accountable.
Explain how salvation through repentance remains consistent with the claim that evildoers receive deserved accountability.
Explain how salvation can forgive repentant sinners without leaving the deserved penalty unpaid.
Explain how forgiveness of a repentant wrongdoer can preserve punishment and divine justice rather than eliminate accountability.
Explain how secular agents can correct widespread inherited moral error through reflective reasoning.
Explain on secular premises how widespread historical moral error can coexist with objective truth and subsequent moral progress.
Show that lack of eternal cosmic significance entails lack of genuine objective significance.
Explain why finite loving and moral action cannot retain value without ultimate reward or punishment.
Identify why lack of eternal cosmic significance does not entail lack of genuine objective value in finite relationships and actions.
